tweet_summary: A viral video claims a 42-year-old mechanic named Mark Delcourt escaped from a U.S. hospital where staff were harvesting organs from patients without family; the tweet endorses it as 'THEY WANT OUR ORGANS.'
why_note_decision: The video is a fabricated mashup: Lead Stories and Snopes both confirm the clips are unrelated footage from a UK underground bunker, a Florida sheriff, and an Egyptian addiction-treatment-center escape. No hospital, location, date, or news report corroborates the story. A note correcting this clear hoax is warranted on a viral (2.8M-impression) post pushing conspiracy.
judge_guidance: PASS if the note (1) states the video is a fabricated/hoax narrative not depicting a real event, (2) makes clear at least one of its specific origins (e.g., the footage is a mashup of unrelated clips from incidents in places like Egypt/UK/US that do not depict organ harvesting), and (3) cites a credible fact-check (Lead Stories, Snopes, AFP, Reuters, or equivalent). FAIL if the note implies the event might be real, hedges that organ harvesting is plausible here, or relies only on absence-of-news arguments without identifying the misuse of footage.
reference_note: The video is a fabricated mashup of unrelated clips from incidents in Egypt, the UK, and the US that do not depict organ harvesting. https://leadstories.com/hoax-alert/2026/01/fact-check-baseless-video-about-mark-delcourts-escape-from-an-organ-harvesting-hospital-is-mashup-of-unrelated-clips.html

fact_check.notes: Two independent fact-checkers (Lead Stories, Snopes) traced footage to a UK bunker, a Florida sheriff, and an Egyptian rehab center escape. No hospital named, no police report, no credible reporting of any such raid.

importance.lens_rationale: 2.8M impressions of a fabricated narrative fueling distrust of hospitals/doctors directly damages public-health norms; correcting viral conspiracy that erodes institutional trust is high-leverage.
